Gerald Metals Sarl Announces Expansion of Swiss Operations

ZURICH, June 18 – Gerald Metals Sarl, a Switzerland-based firm in the metals and mining sector, announced on Tuesday an expansion of its operations in the country, citing strong demand for strategic metals and favorable market conditions.

The company said it will invest approximately CHF 70 million over the next three years to upgrade its logistics hub near Lugano and enhance its trading infrastructure in Geneva. The project will include the installation of advanced material handling systems and the expansion of office space to accommodate a growing workforce.

“The decision to expand our Swiss operations underscores our long-term commitment to the region and our confidence in the global metals market,” said Philippe Laurent, Managing Director of Gerald Metals Sarl, in a statement. “Switzerland’s stability and access to skilled professionals make it an ideal base for our continued growth.”

Industry analysts welcomed the move, noting Switzerland’s established reputation as a center for commodities trading. “This investment is a positive signal for the Swiss metals sector, which has seen steady growth amid robust demand for key minerals,” said Martina Keller, senior analyst at the Swiss Mining Institute.

The Swiss Association of Metalworkers also praised the announcement, highlighting the potential for job creation. “We anticipate increased employment opportunities, particularly in logistics and trade support,” said association president Luca Bernasconi.

Gerald Metals Sarl, which sources, trades and distributes a range of base and precious metals, currently employs more than 120 staff in Switzerland. The expansion is expected to add around 30 new positions by 2026.

Laurent said the company would continue to assess further investment opportunities in the region as market conditions evolve.
